edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 10

source_text: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea. Quantum equitatus Domini differt ab equis Pharaonis, tantum ecclesia differt a filiabus alienis. Pulchrae sunt genae tuae sicut turturis; collum tuum sicut monilia. Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi cum vermiculis argenteis, donec rex accubuerit. Angeli et amici sponsi ornamenta interim parant; cum surrexerit sponsus a passione, ipse aurum et argentum perfectum largietur.
pass_a_gloss: To-cavalry my in chariots of-Pharaoh I-likened you, friend my. By-as-much-as cavalry of-Lord differs from horses of-Pharaoh, by-so-much church differs from daughters alien. Beautiful are cheeks your as of-turtledove; neck your as necklaces...
pass_b_english: [[I have likened you, my friend, to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:9]]. As far as the Lord’s cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses, so far the church differs from alien daughters. [[Your cheeks are beautiful as a turtledove’s; your neck as necklaces >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:10]]. [[We will make you ornaments of gold with studs of silver, until the king reclines >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:11-12]]. Angels and the Bridegroom’s friends prepare ornaments for a time; when the Bridegroom has risen from the passion, he himself will bestow perfect gold and silver.
